1.1:
Love righteousness, you that are rulers of the earth. 
Think of ‎𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 in goodness and seek Him in integrity of heart.
1.2:
For He is found by those who do not try Him, 
And reveals Himself to those who do not distrust Him.
1.3:
For perverse thoughts separate from Elohim, 
And His power, when it is tried, reproves the unwise.
1.4:
For wisdom does not enter into a malicious being, 
Nor dwell in the body that is subject to sin.
1.5:
For the qodesh spirit of discipline flees deceit, 
And turns away from thoughts that are without understanding, 
And does not remain when unrighteousness comes in.
1.6:
For wisdom is a loving spirit, 
But a blasphemer shall not go unpunished for his words. 
For Elohim is witness of his kidneys, 
And a true watcher of his heart, and a hearer of his tongue.
1.7:
For the Ruaḥ of ‎𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 fills the world, 
And that which sustains all knows what is said.
1.8:
Therefore he who speaks unrighteous words is not hidden, 
Nor does vengeance pass him by when it punishes.
1.9:
For a search shall be made into the counsels of the wicked, 
And the words of his voice shall come to ‎𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 to reveal his wicked deeds.
1.10:
For a jealousy ear hears all words, 
And the sound of grumbling is not hidden.
1.11:
Therefore beware of grumbling, which is useless, 
And keep your tongue from secrecy. 
For no secret word is without evil, 
And a lying mouth destroys the being.
1.12:
Do not seek death in the straying of your life, 
And do not pull destruction upon yourself with the works of your hands.
1.13:
For Elohim did not make death, 
Nor does He delight in the destruction of the living.
1.16:
But wicked men with their works and words called it to them, 
For when they thought to have it their friend, they perished to naught, 
And made a covenant with it, 
Because they deserve to receive a share in it.

10.1:
She preserved the first formed father of the world, 
Who was created alone, and brought him out from his fall,
10.2: And gave him power to rule all creatures.
10.3:
But when the unrighteous went away from her in his wrath, 
He also perished in the fury with which he murdered his brother.
10.4:
For whose cause the earth being drowned with the flood, 
Wisdom again preserved it, 
And directed the course of the righteous within a piece of wood of little value.
10.5:
And the nations being confounded in their wicked conspiracy, 
She found out the righteous, 
And preserved him blameless before Elohim, 
And kept him strong despite his tender compassion toward his son.
10.6:
When the wicked perished, she delivered the righteous man, 
Who fled from the fire which fell down upon the five cities.
10.9: But wisdom delivered those who attended to her from pain.
10.10:
When the righteous fled from his brother’s wrath she guided him in right paths, 
Showed him the reign of Elohim, and gave him knowledge of qodesh matters, 
Made him wealthy in his travels, and multiplied the fruit of his labors.
10.11: In the covetousness of those who oppressed him she stood by him, and made him wealthy.
10.13:
When the righteous was sold, she did not forsake him, 
But delivered him from sin: 
She went down with him into the pit,
10.14:
And did not leave him in chains, till she brought him the sceptre of the reign, 
And power against those who oppressed him: 
As for those who had accused him, she showed them to be liars, 
And gave him everlasting esteem.
10.15: She delivered the righteous people and blameless seed from the nation that oppressed them.
10.16:
She entered into the being of the servant of ‎𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, 
And withstood awesome melaḵim with wonders and signs;
10.18:
Brought them through the Sea of Reeds, 
And led them through deep waters.
10.19: But she drowned their enemies, and threw them up from the depth of the sea.
10.20:
Therefore the righteous plundered the wicked, 
And praised Your qodesh Name, O ‎𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, 
And with one accord exalted Your hand, that fought for them.
10.21:
For wisdom opened the mouth of the dumb, 
And taught the tongues of those who could not speak.

11.1: She prospered their works in the hand of the qodesh naḇi.
11.2:
They went through the wilderness that was uninhabited, 
And pitched tents in places where there lay no way.
11.3:
They stood against their enemies, 
And were avenged of their adversaries.
11.4:
When they were thirsty, they called upon You, 
And water was given them out of the flinty rock, 
And their thirst was quenched out of the solid rock.
11.5:
For in what matters their enemies were punished, 
By the same they in their need were benefited.
11.6: For instead of a constant running river troubled with foul blood,
11.7:
For a visible reproof of that command, whereby the infants were slain, 
You gave to them abundance of water by means of which they had no expectancy;
11.8: Revealing by that thirst at that time how you had punished their adversaries.
11.9:
For when they were tried although chastised in kindness, 
They knew how the wicked were judged in wrath and tortured, 
Thirsting in a different manner than the righteous.
11.10:
For these You admonish and try, as a Father, 
But the other, as a severe Meleḵ, You condemn and punish.
11.11:
Whether they were absent or present, 
They were punished alike.
11.12:
For a double grief came upon them, 
And a groaning for the remembrance of what was past.
11.13:
For when they heard through their own punishments the other had benefited, 
They sensed that it was from ‎𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
11.14:
For whom they treated with scorn, 
When he was sent out long before the throwing out of the infants, 
In the end, when they saw what came to be, they admired him.
11.16:
That they might know, that in all the ways a man sins, 
By the same he shall also be punished.
11.17:
For Your Almighty hand, that made the world of formless matter, 
Did not lack the means to send a multitude of bears or fierce lions among them,
11.19:
From which not only the damage might kill them at once, 
But also the terrible sight utterly destroy them.
11.21:
For You show Your great power at all times when you desire; 
And who withstands the strength of Your arm?
11.22:
For the whole world is like a small grain in the balance before You, 
Even as a drop of the morning dew that falls down upon the earth.
11.24:
For You love all that exist, and loathe none whom You have made; 
For You would never have made any matter, if You had hated it.
11.25:
And how could any matter have endured, if it had not been Your desire? 
Or been preserved, if not called by You?
11.26:
But You spare all: for they are Yours, O ‎𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, 
You lover of the living.

12.1: For Your incorruptible Ruaḥ is in all.
12.2:
Therefore little by little You discipline those who offend, 
And warn them by keeping them in remembrance of that in which they have sinned, 
So that turning from their wickedness they believe on You, O ‎𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
12.3: By the hands of our fathers You determined to destroy both those old inhabitants of Your qodesh land,
12.4: Whom You hated for doing most abominable works of witchcraft and wicked slaughterings;
12.5:
And also those cruel murderers of children, 
And devourers of the flesh of man, and the feasts of blood,
12.6:
With their priests from among their idolatrous group, 
And the parents, that killed helpless lives with their own hands;
12.7:
So that the land, which You esteemed above all other, 
Might receive a worthy assembly of children of Elohim.
12.8:
Nevertheless even those You spared, being but men, 
And sent hornets - forerunners of your host – to destroy them little by little.
12.9:
Not that You were unable to bring the wicked under the hand of the righteous in battle, 
Or to destroy them at once with cruel beasts, or with one stern word;
12.10:
But executing Your judgments upon them little by little, 
You gave them place for repentance, not being ignorant that they were a wicked generation, 
And that their evil was inherited, and that their minds could never be changed.
12.11:
For it was a cursed seed from the beginning; 
Neither for fear of any man did You pardon them for those matters in which they sinned.
12.12:
For who shall say, “What have You done?” 
Or who shall withstand Your judgment? 
Or who shall accuse You for the nations that perish, whom You made? 
Or who shall come to stand against You, to be avenged for the unrighteous?
12.13:
For neither is there any Elohim but You that looks after all, 
To whom You might show that Your judgment is not unrighteous.
12.14: Neither shall meleḵ or ruler be able to turn his face against you for any whom You have punished.
12.16:
For Your power is the beginning of righteousness, 
And because You are Aḏon of all, it causes You to show favor to all.
12.17:
For when men shall not believe that You are all powerful, 
You show Your strength, 
And among those who know it You make their boldness manifest.
12.19:
But by such works You have taught Your people that the righteous man should be kind, 
And have prepared Your children with good expectancy that You allow repentance for sins.
12.21:
With what great discernment You rightly ruled Your own children, 
Unto whose fathers You have sworn, 
And made Covenants of good promises?
12.22:
Therefore, whereas You discipline us, 
You scourge our enemies one thousand times more, 
To the intent that, when we judge, we should carefully think of Your goodness, 
And when we ourselves are judged, we should look for kindness.
12.23:
Wherefore, whereas men have lived corruptly and unrighteously, 
You have punished them with their own abominations.
12.24:
For they went very far astray in the ways of straying, 
And upheld for mighty ones, the beasts which even among their enemies were despised, 
Being deceived, as children of no understanding.
12.25:
Therefore unto them, as children without the use of reason, 
You sent a judgment to mock them.
12.26:
But those who would not repent by that correction, in which He scolded them, 
Shall feel a deserved judgment from Elohim.
12.27:
See, for what matters they grumbled, when they were punished, 
That is, from those which they thought to be mighty ones; 
Being punished because of them, when they saw it, 
They acknowledged Him to be the true Elohim, whom before they refused to know: 
And therefore severe judgment came upon them.

13.2:
But supposed either fire, or wind, or the swift air, 
Or the circle of the stars, or the raging water, 
Or the lights of the shamayim to be the mighty ones which govern the world.
13.4:
But if they were astonished at their power and excellence, 
Let them understand by them, how much mightier He is that made them.
13.5: For the greatness and loveliness of the creation is seen in proportion to the maker of them.
13.6:
But yet for this they are the less to be blamed: 
For perhaps they stray, seeking Elohim, 
And desire to find him.
13.7:
For being accompanied with His works they search Him diligently, and believe their sight; 
Because that which is seen is lovely.
13.8: However neither are they to be pardoned.
13.9:
For if they were able to know so much, that they could examine the world; 
How did they not sooner find out the Aḏon of such?
13.10:
But they are miserable, and their expectancy is in dead objects, 
Who call them mighty ones, which are the works of men’s hands, 
Gold and silver fashioned with skill and likeness of beasts, 
Or a stone good for naught - the work of an aged hand.
13.12: And after using the remains of his work to prepare his food, has filled himself;
13.13:
And taking the very waste among that which served no use, 
Being a crooked piece of wood, and full of knots, 
Has carved it diligently, when he had none else to do, 
And formed it by the skill of his knowledge, 
And fashioned it into the image of a man;
13.15:
And when he has made a suitable space for it, 
Positioned it on a wall, and fastened it with iron –
13.17:
Then he makes a prayer for his possessions, for his wife and children, 
And is not ashamed to speak to that which has no life.
13.19:
And for gaining and getting, and for good success of his hands, 
Asks ability to do from that which is most unable to do any deed.

14.1:
Again, one preparing himself to sail, 
And about to pass through the raging waves, 
Calls upon a piece of wood more rotten than the vessel that carries him.
14.2:
For truly this was planned by desire for gain, 
And the workman built it by his skill.
14.3:
But Your providence, O Father, guides it; 
For You have made a path in the sea, and a safe way in the waves;
14.4:
Showing that You save from every danger: 
Even though a man went to sea without regard.
14.5:
Nevertheless You do not want that the works of Your wisdom should be idle, 
And therefore men committing their lives to a small piece of wood, 
And passing the rough sea in a weak vessel are saved.
14.6:
For also in ages past, when the proud giants perished, 
The expectancy of the world governed by Your hand escaped in a weak vessel, 
And left a seed of generation to all ages.
14.7: For the wood by which righteousness comes has received beraḵah.
14.9: For the wicked and his wickedness alike are both hateful to Elohim.
14.10: For that which is made shall be punished together with he who made it.
14.11:
Therefore there shall even be a reckoning upon the idols of the gentiles: 
For in the creation of Elohim they have become an abomination, 
And stumbling-blocks to the beings of men, 
And a snare to the feet of the unwise.
14.12:
For the devising of idols was the beginning of spiritual whoring, 
And the creation of them the corruption of life.
14.13:
For neither were they from the beginning, 
Nor shall they be forever.
14.14:
For by the conceit of men they entered into the world, 
And therefore shall they come quickly to an end.
14.15:
For a father afflicted with untimely mourning, 
When he has made an image of his child soon taken away, 
Now esteemed him as a mighty one, which was then a dead one, 
And delivered to those beneath him ceremonies and offerings.
14.16:
Thus over time an evil custom grew strong being kept as a law, 
And graven images were worshipped by the commands of melaḵim.
14.17:
When men could not esteem in presence, because they dwelt far away, 
They took the likeness of his image from afar, 
And made an exact likeness of a meleḵ whom they esteemed, 
So that through their ardor they might flatter he who was absent, as if he were present.
14.18: The skill of the craftsman also helped to impel the ignorant to increased worship.
14.19:
For he, perhaps willing to please one in authority, 
Forced all his skill to make the likeness in the best fashion.
14.20:
And so the multitude, attracted by the appeal of the work, 
Accepted him now as a mighty one, 
Who a little before was only esteemed.
14.21:
And this was an occasion to deceive the world: 
For men, serving either calamity or authority, 
Ascribed unto stones and stocks the Name not to be shared.
14.23:
For while they slew their children in offerings, 
Or performed secret ceremonies, or held wild festivals of strange rituals;
14.24:
No longer did they keep lives nor marriages undefiled; 
But each one slew another in betrayal, or grieved him through adultery.
14.25:
So that there ruled in all men without exception: 
Blood, murder, theft, and hypocrisy, 
Corruption, unbelief, confusion, falsehood,
14.26:
Distress of good men, forgetfulness of good, defilement of beings, 
Changing of kind, disorder in marriages, adultery, and shameless uncleanness.
14.27: For the worshipping of idols not to be named Is the beginning, the cause, and the end of all evil.
14.28:
For either they rave when they exult, or prophesy lies, 
Or live unrighteously, 
Or else readily contradict themselves.
14.29:
For because their trust is in idols, which have no life; 
Though they swear falsely, yet they expect no harm.
14.30:
However for both causes they shall be rightly punished: 
Both because they did not think well of Elohim, 
Giving heed to idols, and also unrighteously swore in deceit, 
Despising qodeshah.
14.31:
For it is not the power of them by whom they swear: 
But it is the righteous vengeance of sinners, 
That always punishes the offense of the wicked.

15.1:
But you, O Elohim, showing favor and truth, 
Patient, and ruling all in kindness,
15.2:
For if we sin, we are Yours, knowing Your power; 
But we shall not sin, knowing that we are considered Yours.
15.3:
For to know You, is perfect righteousness, 
Also to know Your power is the root of immortality.
15.5:
The sight of which entices fools to lust after it, 
And so they desire the form of a lifeless image that has no breath.
15.6:
Both those who make them, those who desire them, and those who worship them, 
Are lovers of evil, and are worthy to have such to trust upon.
15.7:
For the potter, kneading soft earth, fashions every vessel with much labor for our service; 
Indeed, of the same clay he makes both the vessels that serve for clean uses, 
And likewise also all those who serve the contrary. 
But to what is the use of either, the potter himself is the judge.
15.8:
And using his labors wickedly, he makes a vain mighty one of the same clay, 
Even he which a little before was made of earth himself, 
And within a little while after returns to the same, 
When his life which was loaned to him shall be demanded.
15.9:
But his concern is, not that he shall have much labor, 
Nor that his life is short; 
But strives to outdo goldsmiths and silversmiths, 
And endeavors to do like the workers in bronze, 
And counts it his esteem to make that which is counterfeit.
15.10:
His heart is ashes, his expectancy is cheaper than dirt, 
And his life of less value than clay.
15.11:
Because he did not know his Maker, 
And He who inspired into him an active being, 
And breathed in a living spirit.
15.12:
But they reckoned our life a game, 
And our time here a market-place for gain; 
For they say, “We must acquire every way.” 
Though it be by evil means.
15.13:
For this man, of earthly matter knows he is stumbling above all else, 
Making frail vessels and graven images.
15.14:
And all the enemies of Your people, that hold them in subjection, are most foolish, 
And are more miserable than an infant.
15.16:
For man made them, and he who borrowed his own spirit fashioned them: 
But no man makes a mighty one that is like himself.
15.18:
Also, they worshipped those beasts that are also most hateful; 
For being compared together, some are worse than others.
15.19:
Neither do they look good, so much as to be desired regarding beasts: 
But they went without the praise of Elohim and His beraḵah.

16.1:
Therefore by these they were rightly punished, 
And tortured by a multitude of beasts.
16.3:
So that they, desiring food, 
Due to the ugly sight of the beasts sent among them, 
Might loathe even that which they desired. 
But these, suffering hardship for a short time, 
Might be made partakers of delicacies.
16.4:
For it was necessary, that upon those oppressors suffering should come, which they could not avoid. 
But to these it should only be shown how their enemies were punished.
16.5:
For when the fearful fierceness of beasts came upon them, 
And they perished with the stings of writhing serpents, 
Your wrath did not endure forever.
16.6:
But they were troubled for a little while that they might be warned, 
Receiving a sign of deliverance, to remind them of the Command of Your Law.
16.7:
For he who turned himself toward it was not saved by that which he saw, 
But by You, who are the Savior of all.
16.8:
And in this You made Your enemies confess, 
That it is You who delivers from all evil.
16.9:
For the biting of locusts and flies killed them, 
Neither was there found any healing for their life: 
For they deserved to be punished by such.
16.10:
But Your sons were not overcome by the very fangs of venomous serpents, 
For Your kindness was continually upon them, and healed them.
16.11:
For they were pierced, that they should remember Your Words, 
And were quickly delivered, 
So not to fall into deep forgetfulness, 
That they remember Your goodness.
16.12:
For it was neither herb, nor poultice, that healed them, 
But Your Word, O ‎𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, that heals all.
16.13:
For You have power of life and death. 
You lead to the gates of She’ol, and bring up again.
16.15: But it is impossible to escape Your hand.
16.16:
For the wicked, that denied to know You, 
Were beaten by the strength of Your arm; 
They were pursued with strange rains, hail and showers that they could not avoid, 
And they were consumed by fire.
16.17:
For the fire - which is most astounding - had more force in the water, that quenches all; 
For the world fights for the righteous.
16.19:
And at another time it burns stronger than fire even in the midst of water, 
That it might destroy the increase of an unrighteous land.
16.20:
Instead You fed Your own people with food of messengers, 
And sent them bread from the shamayim prepared without their labor, 
Able to content every delight, and pleasant to every taste.
16.21:
For your sustenance revealed Your sweetness toward Your children, 
And serving to the appetite of the eater, 
Rendered itself to every man’s liking.
16.22:
But snow and ice endured the fire, without melting, 
That they might know that fire burning in the hail, and flashing in the rain, 
Destroyed the increase of their enemies.
16.23:
But this again forgot even its own strength, 
That the righteous might be nourished.
16.24:
For the creation that serves You, the Maker, 
Increases its strength against the unrighteous for their punishment. 
And diminishes its strength for the benefit of those who put their trust in You.
16.27:
For that which was not destroyed by the fire, 
Being warmed with a few rays of sun, soon melted away,
16.28:
That it might be known that we must rise before the sun and give You thanks, 
And pray to you at the daybreak.
16.29:
For the expectancy of the unthankful shall melt away as the winter frost, 
And shall run away as useless water.

17.1:
For Your judgments are great, and cannot be expressed; 
Therefore beings not instructed have strayed.
17.2:
For when unrighteous men thought to oppress the qodesh nation; 
They, being shut up in their houses, the prisoners of darkness, 
And shackled in the bonds of a long night, 
Lay exiled from the anticipation of eternity.
17.3:
For while they thought to lie hidden in their secret sins, 
They were scattered under a dark veil of forgetfulness, 
Being greatly astonished, and troubled with visions.
17.4:
For neither could the corner that held them keep them from fear: 
But noises falling down sounded about them, 
And mournful visions appeared to them with a heavy presence.
17.5:
No power of the fire could give them light: 
Nor could the bright flames of the stars endure to lighten that horrible night.
17.6:
Only a very dreadful fire kindled by itself appeared to them; 
For being greatly afraid, they thought that which they saw to be worse than the sight they did not see.
17.7:
As for the illusions of magic, they were brought to naught, 
And their boasting in wisdom was reproved with shame.
17.8:
For those who promised to drive away fear and troubles from a sick being, 
Were sick themselves of fear, worthy to be laughed at.
17.9:
For though no fearsome matter frightened them; 
Yet being scared of beasts that passed by, and hissing of serpents,
17.10:
They perished from fear, 
Denying that they saw the air, which could in no way be avoided.
17.11:
For wickedness, condemned by her own witness, 
Is very fearful, and being pressured by conscience, always foresees difficulties.
17.12: For fear is naught but a betrayal of the support which reason offers.
17.13:
And the expectation from within, being lesser, 
Counts the ignorance greater than the cause which brings the torment.
17.14:
But they sleeping the same sleep that night, which was indeed unbearable, 
And which came upon them out of the imminent depths of She’ol,
17.16: So then whoever fell down there was thus kept, shut up in a prison without iron bars,
17.17:
For whether he were a farmer, or shepherd, 
Or a laborer in the field, 
He was overtaken, and endured that unavoidable necessity; 
For they were all bound with one chain of darkness.
17.18:
Whether it wore a whistling wind, 
Or a melodious noise of birds among the spreading branches. 
Or a pleasant waterfall running forcefully.
17.19:
Or a terrible sound of stones thrown down, 
Or a stampeding of beasts that could not be seen, 
Or a roaring voice of most savage wild beasts, 
Or a rebounding echo from the hollow mountains; 
These made them to faint for fear.
17.20:
For the whole world shone with radiant light, 
And none were hindered in their labor;

18.1:
Nevertheless, your qodeshim had a very great light, 
Whose voice they heard, but did not see their shape, 
They also counted them happy, for they had not likewise suffered.
18.2:
And because of this, they did not harm those by whom they had been wronged before, they thanked them, 
And pleaded for their forgiveness that they had been enemies.
18.3:
Instead of this You gave them a burning pillar of fire, 
Both to be a guide for the unknown journey, 
And a harmless sun to comfort them in esteem.
18.4:
For they deserved to be deprived of light and imprisoned in darkness, 
Who had kept Your sons imprisoned, 
By whom the incorruptible light of the Law was to be given unto the world.
18.5:
And when they had determined to slay the infants of the qodeshim, 
One child being thrown forth, but saved, 
To reprove them, You took away the multitude of their children, 
And destroyed them altogether in a mighty flood.
18.6:
Of that night our fathers were informed before, 
That knowing with certainty unto what promises they had trusted, 
They might afterwards be of good courage.
18.7:
So both the deliverance of the righteous, 
And destruction of their enemies was accepted by Your people.
18.8:
For by which You punished our adversaries, 
By the same You esteemed us, whom You had called.
18.9:
For the righteous children of good men made offerings secretly, 
And with one accord made a qodesh law, 
That the qodeshim should likewise be partakers of the same good and evil, 
The fathers now singing out the songs of praise.
18.10:
But on the other side was the sound of a despairing cry of the enemies, 
And a grievous noise was spread abroad for children that were bewailed.
18.11:
The master and the servant were punished after one manner; 
And the meleḵ suffered the same as the common person.
18.13:
For although they would not believe by reason of their magic; 
Upon the destruction of the firstborn, they acknowledged these people to be the sons of Elohim.
18.14:
For while all was in quiet silence, 
And that night was in the midst of its swift course,
18.15:
Your mighty Word leaped out of the shamayim from Your royal throne, 
As a fierce man of battle into the midst of a land of destruction,
18.17:
Then suddenly visions of horrible dreams troubled them greatly. 
And fears not sought for came upon them.
18.18:
And one thrown here, and another there half dead, 
Revealed the cause of his death.
18.19:
For the dreams that troubled them forewarned this, 
Lest they should perish, and not know why they were afflicted.
18.21:
For then a blameless man hurried, 
And stood forth to defend them; 
And bringing the shield of his own service, 
Even prayer, and the atonement of incense, 
Opposed the wrath, and brought the calamity to an end, 
Declaring that he was Your servant.
18.22:
So he overcame the destroyer, not with strength of body, 
Nor with force of arms, 
But with a word subdued He who punished, 
Declaring the oaths and Covenants made with the fathers.
18.23:
For when the dead had fallen down in heaps one upon another, 
Standing between, he held back the wrath, 
And parted the way to the living.
18.24:
For in the long garment was the whole world, 
And in the four rows of the stones was engraved the esteem of the fathers, 
And Your excellence upon the turban of his head.
18.25:
To these the destroyer yielded, and feared; 
For it was enough that they only tasted the wrath.

19.1:
As for the wicked, wrath came upon them without kindness to their end; 
For He knew before what they would do;
19.2:
How having allowed them to depart, and sent them away in haste, 
They would reconsider and pursue them.
19.3:
For while they were still mourning and lamenting at the graves of the dead, 
They added another foolish scheme, and pursued as fugitives, 
Those whom they had begged to leave.
19.5:
And that Your people might travel an extraordinary way, 
But they would find a strange death.
19.7:
As a cloud overshadowing the camp. 
And where water stood before, dry land appeared, 
And out of the Sea of Reeds, an unobstructed way; 
And out of the raging river, a green field,
19.8:
Where all the people went through that were defended by Your hand, 
Seeing Your marvelous, awesome wonders.
19.9:
For they reared like horses, and leaped like lambs, 
Praising you, O ‎𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, who had delivered them.
19.10:
For they still remembered what was done while they sojourned in the strange land, 
How the ground brought forth flies instead of cattle, 
And how the river threw up multitudes of frogs instead of fish.
19.11:
But afterwards they saw a new offspring of birds, 
When being led with their appetite, they asked for luxurious meats.
19.12: For quails came up to them from the sea for their satisfaction.
19.13:
And punishments came upon the sinners, 
Not without former signs of the power of thunder; 
For they suffered rightly according to their own wickedness, 
Because they exercised a harder and hateful behavior toward sojourners.
19.14:
For the Seḏomites did not receive those who were unknown when they came, 
But these brought friends into slavery, that deserved good from them.
19.15:
And not only so, but supposed some respect would be had of those, 
Because they treated sojourners hatefully.
19.16:
But they afflicted those grievously, whom they had received with feasting, 
And had already shared in the same laws with them.
19.17:
Therefore they were stricken with blindness, 
As those at the doors of the righteous man; 
When being surrounded with great, horrible darkness, 
Every one sought to pass by his own doors.
19.18:
For the elements were changed in themselves by a kind of harmony, 
As notes change the name of the tune on a harp 
And yet are always sounds; 
Which are understood by the sight of that which has been done.
19.19:
For those of the earth were turned into watery, 
And that which before swam in the water, now moved on the earth.
19.20:
The fire had power in the water, forgetting its own ability; 
And the water forgot its own quenching nature.
19.21:
On the contrary, the flames did not destroy the flesh of the corruptible living matters, though they walked in them; 
Neither melted the frosty food from the shamayim that would naturally melt.
19.22:
For in all matters O ‎𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, 
You exalted Your people and esteemed them, 
Neither did You lightly regard them, 
But assisted them at every time and place.

2.1:
For the wicked, reasoning with themselves, but not rightly said, 
“Our life is short and tedious, 
And of the death of a man there is no healing; 
Neither was there any man known to have returned from the grave.
2.3:
Which being extinguished, our body shall be turned into ashes, 
And our spirit shall vanish as the soft air.
2.4:
“And our name shall be forgotten in time, 
And no man shall remember our works, 
And our life shall pass away as the traces of a cloud, 
And shall be dispersed as a mist, 
That is driven away with the rays of the sun, 
And overcome by its heat.
2.6:
“Come therefore, let us enjoy the good that is found, 
And let us hasten to use the creation as in youth.
2.7:
“Let us fill ourselves with costly wine and ointments, 
And let no flower of the spring pass by us.
2.8: “Let us crown ourselves with rosebuds, before they wither.
2.11:
“Let our strength be the law of righteousness, 
For that which is feeble is found to be worthless.
2.13:
“He professes to have the knowledge of Elohim, 
And calls himself the child of ‎𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄!
2.14: “He has become a reproof to our thoughts.
2.15:
“He is a burden to us to even look at, 
For his life is not like other men, 
His ways are a different way.
2.16:
“We are regarded by him as false, 
He abstains from our ways as from filthiness, 
He pronounces the end of the righteous to be happy, 
And makes his boast that Elohim is his Father!
2.17:
“Let us see if his words are true, 
And let us prove what shall befall him in the end.
2.18:
“For if the righteous man is the son of Elohim, 
He shall help him, and deliver him from the hand of his enemies.
2.19:
“Let us try him with mocking and torture, 
So that we may know his humility, 
And prove his patience.
2.20:
“Let us condemn him with a shameful death; 
For by his own words, he shall be favored.”
2.21:
Such as these they devised, and were deceived; 
For their own wickedness has blinded them.
2.23:
For Elohim created man to be immortal, 
And made him to be an image of His own immortality.
2.24:
Nevertheless death came into the world through envy of the devil, 
And those who hold to His side find it.

3.1:
But the beings of the righteous are in the hand of Elohim, 
And no torture shall touch them.
3.2:
In the eyes of the unwise they seemed to die, 
And their departure is taken for misery,
3.3:
And their going from us to be utter destruction: 
But they are at peace.
3.4:
For though they are punished in the eyes of men, 
Yet their expectancy is full of immortality.
3.5:
And having been discipled a little, they shall be rewarded greatly; 
For Elohim proved them, and found them worthy for Himself.
3.6:
He has tried them as gold in the furnace, 
And received them as a burnt offering.
3.7:
And in the time of their visitation they shall shine, 
And run to and fro like sparks among the stubble.
3.8:
They shall judge the nations, and reign over the people, 
And their Aḏon shall reign forever.
3.10:
But the wicked shall be punished according to their own schemes, 
Who have neglected the righteous, and forsaken ‎𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
3.11:
For whoever despises wisdom and instruction is miserable, 
And their expectancy is vain, their labors unfruitful, 
And their works unprofitable.
3.12: Their wives are foolish, and their children wicked;
3.13:
Their offspring are cursed. 
Therefore ashrĕ is the barren one who is undefiled, 
Who has not known the sinful bed; 
She shall bear fruit in the visitation of lives.
3.14:
And ashrĕ is the eunuch, who has done no evil with his hands, 
Nor devised wickedness against Elohim; 
For unto him shall be given the special gift of belief, 
And an inheritance more desired by his being in the Hĕyḵal of ‎𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
3.15:
For the fruit of good labors is esteemed, 
And the root of wisdom shall never fail.
3.16:
As for the children of adulterers, they shall not come to their perfection, 
And the seed of an unrighteous bed shall be uprooted.
3.17:
For though they live long, yet they shall be regarded as naught, 
And their end shall be without esteem.
3.18:
Or, if they die quickly, they have no expectancy, 
Nor comfort in the day of trial.
3.19: For the end of the unrighteous generation is terrible.

4.2:
When it is present, men take example from it; 
And when it is gone, they desire it. 
It wears a crown, and overcomes forever, 
Having overcome, striving for undefiled rewards.
4.3:
But the multiplying brood of the wicked shall not thrive, 
Nor take deep root by illegitimate seed, 
Nor lay any lasting foundation.
4.5:
The imperfect branches shall be broken off, 
Their fruit unprofitable - not ripe to eat, 
Also of no use.
4.6: For children brought forth by lawless beds are witnesses of wickedness against their parents in their trial.
4.7:
But though the righteous be prevented by death, 
Yet he shall be at rest.
4.8:
For esteemed age is not that which stands in length of time, 
Nor measured by number of years.
4.9:
But wisdom is the grey hair unto men, 
And an unstained life is old age.
4.10:
He pleased Elohim, and was loved by Him; 
So that living among sinners he was translated.
4.11:
Indeed, was he taken away speedily, 
Lest wickedness should alter his understanding, 
Or deceit deceive his being.
4.12:
For the enticement of greed obscures that which is honest; 
And the wandering of desire undermines the simple minded.
4.13: He, being made perfect in a short time, filled a long time;
4.14:
For his being pleased 
‎𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, Therefore He hastened to take him away from among the wicked.
4.15:
This the people saw, but did not understand, 
Neither did they lay up this in their minds: 
That His favor and kindness is with His qodeshim, 
And that He shows respect to His chosen.
4.17:
For they shall see the end of the wise, 
And shall not understand what Elohim in His counsel has decreed for Him, 
And to what end ‎𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 has put Him in safety.
4.18:
They shall see Him, and despise Him; 
But Elohim shall laugh them to scorn. 
And from then on they shall be an insignificant carcass, 
And a reproach among the dead forever.
4.20:
And when they draw up the account of their sins, they shall come with fear; 
And their own wickednesses shall convict them to their face.

5.1: Then the righteous shall stand in great boldness before the face of those who have afflicted Him, and taken no account of His works.
5.2: When they see it, they shall be troubled with awesome fear, and shall be amazed at the mystery of His deliverance, so far beyond all that they looked for.
5.3: And they, repenting and groaning for anguish of spirit, shall say within themselves, “This was He, whom we once mocked, and a proverb of reproach.
5.4: “We fools accounted His ḥai madness, and His end to be without esteem.
5.5: “How is He numbered among the children of Elohim, and His lot is among the qodeshim?
5.6: “Therefore we have strayed from the Way of truth, and the light of righteousness has not shined upon us, and the brilliance of righteousness did not rise upon us.
5.7: “We wearied ourselves in the way of wickedness and destruction; we have also gone through deserts where there was no path; but as for the Way of ‎𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, we have not known it.
5.8: “What has pride profited us, or what good has wealth with our boasting brought us?”
5.9:
All these have passed away like a shadow, 
And as a rumor that hastened away.
5.10:
And as a ship that passes over the waves of the water, 
Which when it has passed, the trace of it is unable to be found, 
Neither the pathway of the keel in the waves.
5.11:
Or as when a bird has flown through the air, 
There is no sign of its way to be found, 
But the air being lightly beaten with the stroke of its wings and parted with the rapid noise and motion of them is passed through; 
And after passing there is no sign of it to be found.
5.12:
Or as when an arrow is shot at a mark, 
It parts the air, which immediately comes together again, 
So one cannot know where it went through.
5.13:
Even so, we also, as soon as we were born, 
Began to draw to our end and had no sign of uprightness to show, 
But were consumed in our wickedness.
5.16:
Therefore they shall receive an esteemed reign, and a lovely crown from the hand of ‎𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄: 
For with His right hand He shall cover them, 
And with His arm He shall protect them.
5.17:
He shall take his ardor as complete armor, 
And make creation His weapon for the vengeance of His enemies.
5.18:
He shall put on righteousness as a breastplate, 
And true judgment in place of a helmet.
5.19: He shall take qodeshah for an invincible shield.
5.20:
He shall sharpen His severe wrath as a sword, 
And the earth shall fight with Him against the foolish.
5.22:
And hailstones filled with wrath shall be thrown as a stone out of bow, 
And the water of the sea shall rage against them, 
And the floods shall cruelly drown them.
5.23:
A mighty wind shall also stand up against them, 
And blow them away like a storm: 
So wickedness shall lay waste the whole earth, 
And evil works shall overthrow the thrones of the mighty.

6.1:
Hear therefore, O you melaḵim, and understand; 
Learn, you who are judges to the ends of the earth.
6.2:
Listen, you who rule the people, 
And boast in the multitude of nations.
6.3:
For power is given to you from ‎𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, 
And rulership from the Most High, 
Who shall try your works, and search out your purposes.
6.5:
He shall come upon you terribly and speedily; 
For a sharp judgment shall be to those who are in high places.
6.6:
For kindness shall soon pardon the harshest, 
But great men shall be greatly tortured.
6.7:
For He who is Aḏon over all shall show no partiality, 
Neither shall he stand in awe of any man’s greatness; 
For he has made the small and great, 
And is concerned for all alike.
6.8: But a severe trial shall come upon the mighty.
6.9:
I speak unto you therefore, O melaḵim, 
That you may learn wisdom, and not fall away.
6.10:
For those who guard qodeshah righteously shall be judged qodesh; 
And those who have learned such matters shall find what to answer.
6.11:
Therefore lay your heart upon my words; 
Desire them, and you shall be instructed.
6.12:
Wisdom is esteemed, and never fades away: 
Also, she is easily seen by those who love her, 
And found by those who seek her.
6.13:
She prevents those who desire her, 
In making herself first known to them.
6.14:
Whoever seeks her early shall have no great hardship: 
For he shall find her sitting at his doors.
6.15:
Therefore to think upon her is perfection of wisdom; 
And whoever watches for her shall quickly be without worry.
6.16:
For she goes about seeking those who are worthy of her, 
Showing herself favorably to those in the Way, 
And meets them in every thought.
6.17:
For the very true beginning of her is the desire of discipline; 
And the concern of discipline is love;
6.18: And love is the keeping of her Laws; and guarding her Laws is the assurance of incorruption;
6.19: And incorruption makes us near to Elohim:
6.20: Therefore the desire of wisdom leads to a reign.
6.21:
If your delight then is in thrones and scepters, 
O rulers of the people, esteem wisdom, 
That you may reign for forever.
6.22:
As for wisdom, what she is, and how she came to be, 
I shall tell you, and shall not hide mysteries from you; 
But shall seek her out from the beginning of her creation, 
And bring the knowledge of her into light, 
And shall not pass over the truth.
6.23:
Neither shall I go with consuming envy; 
For such a man shall have no fellowship with wisdom.
6.24:
But the multitude of the wise is the welfare of the world: 
And a wise meleḵ is the upholding of the people.
6.25:
Receive therefore instruction through my words, 
And it shall do you good.

7.1:
I myself am also a mortal man like all, 
And the offspring of he who was first made from the earth.
7.2:
And was fashioned in my mother’s womb to be flesh in the time of ten months, 
Being compacted in blood, of the seed of man, 
And the pleasure that came with sleep.
7.3:
And when I was born, I drew in the common air, 
And fell upon the earth, which is of like nature, 
And the first voice which I uttered was crying, as all others do.
7.4: I was nursed with compassion, and wrapped in garments.
7.5: For there is no meleḵ that had any other beginning of birth.
7.6:
For all men have one entrance into life, 
And the same going out.
7.7:
Therefore I prayed, and understanding was given to me. 
I called upon Elohim, and the spirit of wisdom came to me.
7.8:
I preferred her before scepters and thrones, 
And deemed wealth naught in comparison to her.
7.9:
Neither did I compare her to any precious stone, 
Because all gold in respect to her is as a little sand, 
And silver is counted as clay before her.
7.11:
All good came to me together with her, 
And much wealth in her hands.
7.12:
And I rejoiced in them all, because wisdom goes before them; 
And I did not know that she was the mother of them.
7.13:
I learned diligently, and speak of her freely. 
I do not hide her wealth,
7.16:
For in His hand are both we and our words; 
All wisdom also, and knowledge of workmanship.
7.17:
For He has given me certain knowledge of that which exists, 
Namely, to know how the world was made, 
And the operation of the elements.
7.19: The circuits of years, and the positions of stars.
7.21: And all that which is either secret or revealed, these I know.
7.22:
For wisdom, which is the worker of all matters, taught me; 
For in her is an understanding spirit: qodesh, unique, manifold, wise, lively, clear, undefiled, clean, strong, loving the good, alive, irresistible, ready to do good,
7.23: kind to man, steadfast, sure, free from worry, all powerful, overseeing all, and penetrating all spirits most wise, understanding, and pure.
7.24:
For wisdom is more moving than any motion: 
She passes and penetrates all because of her purity.
7.26:
For she is the brightness of the everlasting Light, 
The unspotted reflection of the power of Elohim, 
And an image of His goodness.
7.27:
And although one, she does all matters: 
And remaining in herself, she renews all matters. 
And entering into qodesh beings of all generations, 
She makes them friends of Elohim, and neḇi’im.
7.28: For Elohim loves none but he who dwells with wisdom.
7.29:
For she is more lovely than the sun, 
And above all the order of stars: 
Compared with the light, she is found before it.
7.30:
For after this comes night, 
But evil shall not prevail against wisdom.

8.1:
Wisdom reaches from one end to another mightily; 
And she rightly orders all matters.
8.2:
I loved her, and sought her out from my youth, 
I desired to make her my bride, and I was a lover of her comeliness.
8.3:
She increases her nobility for she accompanies Elohim; 
Indeed, the Aḏon of all loved her.
8.4:
For she knows the secrets of the knowledge of Elohim, 
And is a lover of His works.
8.5:
If wealth is a possession to be desired in this life; 
What is wealthier than wisdom, the doer of all?
8.6:
And if insight works; 
Who of all that is a more skilled worker than she?
8.8:
If a man desires much experience, she knows the ways of old, 
And concludes rightly what is to come: 
She knows the wisdom of words, and expounds hidden riddles. 
She foresees signs and wonders, and the events of seasons and times.
8.9:
Therefore I purposed to take her to me to live with me, 
Knowing that she would be a counsellor of good, 
And a comfort in worries and grief.
8.10:
Because of her I have esteem among the multitude, 
And esteem with the elders, although I am young.
8.11:
I shall be found alert in judgment, 
And shall be admired in the sight of great men.
8.13:
And by the means of her I shall obtain immortality, 
And leave an everlasting remembrance behind me to those that come after me.
8.14:
I shall put the people in order, 
And the nations shall be subject to me.
8.19: For I was a lively child, and had a good spirit.
8.20: Indeed, being good, I came into a body undefiled.

9.1: “O Elohim of my fathers, and Aḏon of kindness, who has made all by Your Word,
9.2:
and ordained man through Your wisdom, 
That he should reign over the creatures which You have made.
9.3:
“And order the world according to straightness and righteousness, 
And execute right-ruling with an upright heart:
9.4:
“Give me wisdom, that sits by Your throne; 
And do not reject me from among your children.
9.5:
“For I, Your servant and son of Your female servant am a weak man, and short-lived, 
And too young for the understanding of Right-Ruling and Laws.
9.6:
“For though a man be ever so perfect among the children of men, 
Yet if Your wisdom is not with him, he shall be regarded as naught.
9.7:
“You have chosen me to be a meleḵ of Your people, 
And a judge of Your sons and daughters.
9.8:
“You have commanded me to build a Hĕyḵal upon Your qodesh mountain, 
And an altar in the city in which You dwell, 
A resemblance of the qodesh Mishkan, which You have prepared from the beginning.
9.9:
“And wisdom was with You; who knows Your works, 
And was present when You made the world, 
And knew what was acceptable in Your sight, 
And right by Your Commands.
9.10:
“O send her out of Your qodesh shamayim, 
And from the throne of Your esteem, 
That being present she may labor with me, 
That I may know what is pleasing to You.
9.11:
“For she knows and understands all matters, 
And she shall lead me sensibly in my doings, 
And preserve me in her power.
9.12:
“So shall my works be acceptable, 
And then shall I judge Your people righteously, 
And be worthy to sit in my father’s seat.”
9.13:
For what man is he who knows the counsel of Elohim? 
Or who knows the desire of ‎𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄?
9.14:
“For the thoughts of mortal men are wretched, 
And our plans are of uncertainty.
9.15:
For the corruptible body presses down the being, 
And this earthly tent weighs down the mind that thinks upon many matters.
9.17:
And Your counsel who has known, except You give wisdom, 
And send Your Ruaḥ ha’Qodesh from above?
9.18:
For so the ways of those who lived on the earth were instructed, 
And men were taught that which is pleasing to You, 
And were saved through wisdom.
